<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

In NIXL host-buffer mode (TPU, or `kv_buffer_device="cpu"`), a chunked prefill that ends inside a block leaves that block for the next chunk to finish, but the block is never copied to the host buffer again. The decode instance (D) then reads stale KV for up to `block_size - 1` tokens per chunk boundary, with no error. This PR makes `_build_save_meta` (`nixl/base_scheduler.py`) select blocks by token position, so the straddling block is copied again once it is complete.

## Claims

- Each chunk copies the blocks covering `[saved, num_computed + num_scheduled)`. A block that straddles a chunk boundary falls in both ranges, so it is copied again once complete. Example (block size 16, budget 24, 40-token prompt): on main, step 1 copies b0 and b1 with b1 half written, and step 2 copies only b2, so tokens 24-31 never reach the host buffer; with this PR, step 2 copies b1 and b2.
- Spec-decode lookahead blocks are copied only once written (ovidiusm's review).
- A first chunk after a local prefix-cache hit still copies the cached blocks.
- A preempted request starts over when it comes back. It arrives with its whole block table (`is_full_table`, from #60810), so the saved count resets.
- Chunked local attention groups are saved by position too (xuechendi's review). A `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group needs nothing extra: `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` gives the scheduler one of its layer specs, which already takes this path.
- SSM state with `mamba_cache_mode="none"`: each chunk rewrites the state block in place, but main copied it only when allocated, so D got the state after chunk 1. The last chunk now copies the slot that `request_finished` hands to D. The hybrid test from snadampal's review found this, and since it is the same bug I fixed it here; I can split it out if you prefer.

## Validation

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest <the 10 NIXL unit files below> -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

On this branch (Linux CPU): `test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py` 13 passed. With main's `nixl/base_scheduler.py` (8321d1119b), all 9 new test cases fail, 6 of them on what they check (the other 3 also read `_reqs_save_state`, which main doesn't have):

```
resaves_block_straddling_chunk_boundary[40-24-0]:  assert 3 == 2              (straddling block not copied again)
resaves_block_straddling_chunk_boundary[20-18-0]:  KeyError: 'id-1'           (same, second shape: nothing saved in step 2)
resaves_block_straddling_chunk_boundary[40-30-3]:  assert [1, 2, 3] == [1, 2] (lookahead block copied before it is written)
hybrid_attention_and_mamba:                        assert [4] == [2, 4]       (hybrid model: the straddling attention block)
straddling_block_of_other_attention_groups[uniform_type]:  assert [3] == [2, 3]
straddling_block_of_other_attention_groups[chunked_local]: assert [3] == [2, 3]
```

With the last-chunk SSM copy turned off, the hybrid test fails with `assert [] == [3]`. With `is_full_table` ignored, both preemption cases fail with `assert [2, 1] == [1, 2, 3]`. Without the `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec` line in this branch's change, the `[chunked_local]` case fails the same way and `[uniform_type]` passes.

The 10 NIXL unit files: 721 passed, 3 failed; on main (8321d1119b), 712 passed and the same 3 failed (two start a real engine, one needs a gated Hub config).

<details><summary>The files and the 3 failures</summary>

Files: `test_remote_decode_lifecycle`, `test_remote_prefill_lifecycle`, `test_nixl_connector`, `test_nixl_push_connector`, `test_nixl_connector_hma`, `test_bidirectional_kv_transfer`, `test_nixl_heartbeat`, `test_nixl_desc_geometry`, `test_nixl_simple_cpu_offload`, `test_handshake_pp_aggregation`.

Failures, on both: `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]` and `[None]` (real engine), `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` (gated Hub config).

</details>

CI: `test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py` is marked `cpu_test`, so the CPU step runs it. The GPU "V1 KV Connectors" step is disabled on main, so the other NIXL files don't run in CI.

No GPU or TPU run and no evals. The end-to-end check would be `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh --kv_buffer_device cpu` with a `--max-num-batched-tokens` that is not a multiple of the block size, on main and on this branch; I don't have the hardware for it. Outputs change only where the transfer was wrong.

## Details

`_build_save_meta` keeps, per partially prefilled request, its block table per KV cache group and the number of tokens already saved (`_reqs_save_state`), and drops them when the last chunk is scheduled or the request is aborted. `saved` starts at 0, which is why a prefix-cache hit's blocks are copied with the first chunk.

Not covered here, and unchanged from main (they keep main's per-step copy):

- SSM groups with `mamba_cache_mode="align"` (prefix caching on). Their block table is not append-only, as `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` notes, so the state slot can't be found by position.
- `CircularBufferSpec` groups: one ring block per request, rewritten in place, so not positional. If D needs the ring as of the last chunk, it wants the same last-chunk copy as the SSM state; I'd do that as a follow-up with a DSv4.1 test.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes `_build_save_meta` (#60181 changes the receive path).

## AI assistance

AI-assisted; reviewed and tested by me.

Thanks, this is a real silent-corruption fix for host-buffer mode, which we also use on XPU, and the tests cover the shapes well (I confirmed the 7 new tests fail on main and pass here).

One question: `_save_block_size` (base_scheduler.py:171) only recognises `FullAttentionSpec`/`SlidingWindowSpec`, so `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups (mixed head sizes, same attention type) and `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec` fall to the "new blocks only" branch (:511) and keep the straddling-block bug. Should they be keyed by token position too? If they are intentionally excluded, a short comment there would help.

Minor: `SchedulerOutput.preempted_req_ids` is documented as "Only used for v2 model runner"; the connector now relies on it too, so maybe update that comment.

@xuechendi Thanks for checking the tests on main.

- `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`: the connector scheduler gets the scheduler's KV cache config, where `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` replaces each such group with one of its layer specs. So `_save_block_size` already sees a `FullAttentionSpec` (or `MLAAttentionSpec`, `SlidingWindowSpec`) there. The new `[uniform_type]` case of `test_host_buffer_save_resaves_straddling_block_of_other_attention_groups` builds the group through that function.
- `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec`: you're right, it took the new-blocks-only path and kept the bug. Its blocks hold token positions like sliding window, so 8ec63ec0b adds it to the positional specs, with the `[chunked_local]` case of the same test (on main: `assert [3] == [2, 3]`).
- `preempted_req_ids`: 8ec63ec0b also drops the connector's use of it. Since #60810 a preempted request comes back with `is_full_table=True`, which already restarts its save, so that docstring stays accurate.

`CircularBufferSpec` groups stay on the per-step copy: one ring block per request, rewritten in place. If D needs the ring as of the last chunk, I'd add the SSM-style last-chunk copy in a follow-up with a DSv4.1 test.

@NickLucche could you take a look when you have time? In host-buffer mode, D reads stale KV for a block that straddles a chunk boundary; xuechendi confirmed the new tests fail on main. ovidiusm approved before 8ec63ec (`ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec`, xuechendi's question), and snadampal's two test asks are in 753e252.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Have you considered and tested speculative decoding case?

I am not sure if/how this is supported on TPU, but I assume a chunk may allocate a block beyond the one it writes into ([kv_cache_manager.py#L533-L536](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/73a3e1a66469a61e03a00cd9034bdac96cb6886d/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L533-L536)). _reqs_save_tail then stores that look-ahead block, not the partly written one, as you expect here.

Selecting the blocks by token position would avoid this, e.g. blocks[num_computed // block_size : cdiv(num_computed + num_scheduled, block_size)] or something on those lines.

There is a test spec_decode_acceptance_test.sh but depending on prompt size it might not catch the issue.

It would be good to investigate and add a unit test for it.
Could you add unit tests for (1) preempt then resume case and (2) a hybrid (attention + mamba) case?

 import pytest
-
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec,
+    FullAttentionSpec,
+    KVCacheConfig,
+    KVCacheGroupSpec,
+    UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs,
+)
 from vllm.v1.outputs import EMPTY_MODEL_RUNNER_OUTPUT, KVConnectorOutput
 from vllm.v1.request import FinishReason, RequestStatus
 
@@ -13,6 +22,7 @@
     create_request,
     create_scheduler,
     create_vllm_config,
+    make_kv_cache_config,
 )
 
 pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
@@ -260,3 +270,265 @@ def test_abort_during_kv_transfer():
     )
     scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, model_runner_output)
     assert_scheduler_empty(scheduler)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "num_tokens,token_budget,num_lookahead_tokens",
+    [
+        (40, 24, 0),  # chunk 2 = tokens 24..39: rest of b1 plus b2
+        (20, 18, 0),  # chunk 2 = tokens 18..19: fits in b1, no new block
+        (40, 30, 3),  # spec decode: chunk 1 also allocates lookahead block b2
+    ],
+)
+def test_host_buffer_save_resaves_block_straddling_chunk_boundary(
+    num_tokens: int, token_budget: int, num_lookahead_tokens: int
+):
+    """Host-buffer mode (kv_buffer_device="cpu") copies each prefill step's
+    blocks to host memory. When a chunk boundary is not block aligned, the
+    next chunk writes the rest of the previous chunk's last block, so that
+    block must be copied again. Blocks allocated ahead of the written tokens
+    (spec-decode lookahead) must not be copied before they are written."""
+    block_size = 16
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=token_budget,
+        kv_role="kv_producer",
+    )
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(vllm_config)
+    scheduler.num_lookahead_tokens = num_lookahead_tokens
+    connector_scheduler = scheduler.get_kv_connector().connector_scheduler
+    connector_scheduler.use_host_buffer = True
+    request = create_request(
+        request_id=1,
+        num_tokens=num_tokens,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        do_remote_decode=True,
+    )
+    req_id = request.request_id
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    out1 = scheduler.schedule()
+    (saved1,) = out1.kv_connector_metadata.reqs_to_save[req_id].local_block_ids
+    (table,) = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)
+    # Only the blocks holding tokens written in chunk 1.
+    assert saved1 == table[: -(-token_budget // block_size)]
+    model_output = create_model_runner_output([request])
+    model_output.sampled_token_ids = [[]]
+    scheduler.update_from_output(out1, model_output)
+    assert request.num_computed_tokens % block_size != 0
+    first = request.num_computed_tokens // block_size
+    straddling = table[first]
+
+    out2 = scheduler.schedule()
+    (saved2,) = out2.kv_connector_metadata.reqs_to_save[req_id].local_block_ids
+    (table,) = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)
+    assert saved2[0] == straddling
+    assert saved2 == table[first : -(-num_tokens // block_size)]
+    assert req_id not in connector_scheduler._reqs_need_save
+    assert req_id not in connector_scheduler._reqs_save_state
+
+
+def test_host_buffer_save_includes_prefix_cache_hit_blocks():
+    """A first chunk that starts after a local prefix-cache hit still copies
+    the cached blocks: D pulls the whole prompt from the host buffer."""
+    block_size = 16
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=64,
+        kv_role="kv_producer",
+    )
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(vllm_config)
+    connector_scheduler = scheduler.get_kv_connector().connector_scheduler
+    connector_scheduler.use_host_buffer = True
+
+    # Request 1 computes and caches a 32-token (2-block) prefix.
+    first = create_request(
+        request_id=1,
+        num_tokens=40,
+        common_prefix_len=32,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        do_remote_decode=True,
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(first)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_v2_model_runner", [False, True])
+def test_host_buffer_save_restarts_after_preemption(use_v2_model_runner: bool):
+    """Preemption between prefill chunks frees the request's blocks. When it is
+    scheduled again (as a resumed request with the V1 model runner, as a new
+    one with V2), every block it covers is copied again from token 0."""
+    block_size = 16
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=24,
+        kv_role="kv_producer",
+    )
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(vllm_config)
+    scheduler.use_v2_model_runner = use_v2_model_runner
+    connector_scheduler = scheduler.get_kv_connector().connector_scheduler
+    connector_scheduler.use_host_buffer = True
+    request = create_request(
+        request_id=1,
+        num_tokens=40,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        do_remote_decode=True,
+    )
+    req_id = request.request_id
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    out1 = scheduler.schedule()
+    model_output = create_model_runner_output([request])
+    model_output.sampled_token_ids = [[]]
+    scheduler.update_from_output(out1, model_output)
+    scheduler.running.remove(request)
+    scheduler._preempt_request(request, 0.0)
+
+    out2 = scheduler.schedule()
+    if use_v2_model_runner:
+        assert [r.req_id for r in out2.scheduled_new_reqs] == [req_id]
+    else:
+        assert out2.scheduled_cached_reqs.resumed_req_ids == {req_id}
+    (saved2,) = out2.kv_connector_metadata.reqs_to_save[req_id].local_block_ids
+    (table,) = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)
+    assert saved2 == table[: -(-40 // block_size)]
+    assert req_id not in connector_scheduler._reqs_save_state

+def test_host_buffer_save_hybrid_attention_and_mamba():
+    """Hybrid model with mamba_cache_mode="none" (one SSM state block per
+    request). The attention group is saved by token position, so the block
+    straddling the chunk boundary is copied again. Every chunk rewrites the SSM
+    state block in place, so the last chunk must copy it."""

+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=token_budget,
+        max_model_len=max_model_len,
+        kv_role="kv_producer",
+    )
+    vllm_config.scheduler_config.disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager = False
+    vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching = False
+    kv_cache_config = make_kv_cache_config(
+        block_size, mamba_enabled=True, mamba_block_size=max_model_len
+    )
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(
+        vllm_config,
+        kv_cache_config=kv_cache_config,
+        scheduler_block_size=max_model_len,
+    )
+    connector_scheduler = scheduler.get_kv_connector().connector_scheduler
+    connector_scheduler.use_host_buffer = True
+    request = create_request(
+        request_id=1,
+        num_tokens=num_tokens,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        do_remote_decode=True,
+    )
+    req_id = request.request_id
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    out1 = scheduler.schedule()
+    attn1, _ = out1.kv_connector_metadata.reqs_to_save[req_id].local_block_ids
+    attn_table, ssm_table = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req_id)
+    assert attn1 == attn_table[: -(-token_budget // block_size)]

+    out2 = scheduler.schedule()

+    )

inline_comments.body: Thanks, I added both (`test_host_buffer_save_restarts_after_preemption` for the V1 and V2 model runners, and `test_host_buffer_save_hybrid_attention_and_mamba`), and both found a bug, fixed in 753e2523eb. The preemption one is a regression I introduced in fc532ad5d: with the V2 model runner a preempted request comes back in `scheduled_new_reqs`, not as a resumed request, so the save state from before preemption was reused and the wrong blocks were copied. V1 and main were not affected, and the state is now dropped for `scheduler_output.preempted_req_ids`. The hybrid one is not from this PR, main has it too: with `mamba_cache_mode="none"` every chunk rewrites the SSM state block in place, but it was copied only when allocated, so the host buffer kept the state after the first chunk. Since it is the same bug this PR fixes for attention blocks, I fixed it here: the last chunk now copies the SSM state slot that `request_finished` hands to D. Could you take another look?

Thanks, this is a real silent-corruption fix for host-buffer mode, which we also use on XPU, and the tests cover the shapes well (I confirmed the 7 new tests fail on main and pass here).

One question: `_save_block_size` (base_scheduler.py:171) only recognises `FullAttentionSpec`/`SlidingWindowSpec`, so `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups (mixed head sizes, same attention type) and `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec` fall to the "new blocks only" branch (:511) and keep the straddling-block bug. Should they be keyed by token position too? If they are intentionally excluded, a short comment there would help.

Minor: `SchedulerOutput.preempted_req_ids` is documented as "Only used for v2 model runner"; the connector now relies on it too, so maybe update that comment.

@xuechendi Thanks for checking the tests on main.

- `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`: the connector scheduler gets the scheduler's KV cache config, where `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` replaces each such group with one of its layer specs. So `_save_block_size` already sees a `FullAttentionSpec` (or `MLAAttentionSpec`, `SlidingWindowSpec`) there. Have you considered and tested speculative decoding case?

I am not sure if/how this is supported on TPU, but I assume a chunk may allocate a block beyond the one it writes into ([kv_cache_manager.py#L533-L536](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/73a3e1a66469a61e03a00cd9034bdac96cb6886d/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L533-L536)). _reqs_save_tail then stores that look-ahead block, not the partly written one, as you expect here.

Selecting the blocks by token position would avoid this, e.g. blocks[num_computed // block_size : cdiv(num_computed + num_scheduled, block_size)] or something on those lines.

There is a test spec_decode_acceptance_test.sh but depending on prompt size it might not catch the issue.

It would be good to investigate and add a unit test for it.
